target_name: Years Spent in the Trap Corner
rationale: Joint-occupancy duration is a genuinely different construct from the archive's "Chronically Cheap with Heavy Claims" (which used cheapness duration times contemporaneous leverage), but the economic mechanism is the same one and the coarse 0–5 integer output plus a hard non-industry-adjusted 0.6 leverage cutoff will make portfolio extremes lumpy and sector-concentrated, so the upside over the parent is likely modest.

target_name: Cheapness Duration with Claims and Tail Loss
rationale: This is a mechanical blend of two existing archive signals (duration leg from "Chronically Cheap with Heavy Claims," tail-loss leg from "Cheap with Deep Tail Loss") with no new economic channel, and since leverage and cumulative tail losses are both proxies for the same solvency impairment the SUMRANK mostly double-counts rather than adding separable information.

The stated mechanism is interest-plus-depreciation fixed charges, but (ebitda − pi)/sale also absorbs special items and, critically, becomes large precisely when pi is deeply negative, so the leg is substantially a low-profitability/loss sort rather than a capital-structure-commitment measure — making it both internally inconsistent with the hypothesis and overlapping the archive's several cheap-times-unprofitability tests.

Isolating the non-current, non-funded-debt liability residual (pension, deferred tax, other accruals) is a coherent and genuinely under-tested decomposition that sits outside both the current-ratio and the leverage measures already tried, though the residual can be noisy or negative and will partly proxy capital intensity.

Growth in non-cash current assets scaled by sales is close to the well-published accruals / net-operating-asset-growth anomaly, so the distress leg is a known effect rather than a new channel, and the claimed complementarity with the accelerating working-capital-drain signal is questionable since rising receivables and inventory *increase* working capital, giving the two constructs partially opposing loadings on the same variable.

target_name: Cheap Level with Signed Deleveraging News
rationale: The diagnosis of the momentum contamination in "Cheapening Without Distress News" is correct, but the resulting expression is essentially the leverage-change half of the already-tested "Cheap with Twin Deterioration" with the profitability-change leg dropped and the sign flipped, and multiplying a strictly positive rank by a signed z-score means the extreme portfolios will be dominated by outlier delta-leverage observations in small, unstable firms.
